name: Venous Thoracic Outlet Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Venous Thoracic Outlet Syndrome

criteria.description: Unilateral upper extremity swelling and cyanosis
Imaging evidence of subclavian vein thrombosis (e.g., venography, ultrasound)
Positive provocative maneuvers reproducing symptoms (e.g., Adson’s test, Roos test)
Exclusion of other causes of upper extremity deep vein thrombosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of unilateral upper extremity swelling with imaging-confirmed subclavian vein thrombosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by clinical presentation and exclusion of other thrombosis causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral upper extremity venous congestion with cyanosis
searchTerms: one arm with blue discoloration and vein swelling
venous congestion and cyanosis in one arm

pathognomonic.symptomName: Subclavian vein thrombosis confirmed by imaging
searchTerms: blood clot in subclavian vein confirmed by scan
imaging showing vein thrombosis under collarbone
swelling and puffiness of the arm

common.symptomName: Dilated superficial veins over the shoulder and chest wall (collateral veins)
searchTerms: enlarged surface veins on shoulder and chest
visible collateral veins over upper body

common.symptomName: Pain and heaviness in the affected upper limb
searchTerms: pain and heavy feeling in affected arm
aching and weight sensation in limb

common.symptomName: Venous distension exacerbated by arm elevation or activity
searchTerms: vein swelling worsened by raising arm or activity
increased venous pressure with arm elevation

occasional.symptomName: Paresthesia or numbness in the affected arm
searchTerms: loss of sensation or pins and needles in arm

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue or weakness of the affected limb
searchTerms: tiredness or weakness in affected limb

occasional.symptomName: Warmth and erythema of the affected limb

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary embolism secondary to venous thrombosis
searchTerms: lung blood clot from leg thrombosis
lung clot secondary to vein clots

rare.symptomName: Chronic venous insufficiency with skin changes
searchTerms: skin thickening from poor vein flow

rare.symptomName: Muscle atrophy of the upper limb due to chronic venous congestion
searchTerms: arm muscle loss from vein issues

laboratory: Elevated D-dimer may be present but is nonspecific
Normal coagulation profile unless underlying thrombophilia
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing subclavian vein thrombosis
Venography demonstrating venous obstruction or thrombosis
CT or MR venography for anatomical assessment
genetic: No specific genetic markers; thrombophilia screening may be indicated
other: Positive provocative maneuvers (e.g., Adson’s, Roos test)
History of repetitive upper limb activity or trauma

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of venous thrombosis on imaging
Presence of arterial ischemic symptoms (coldness, pallor)
Imaging showing arterial compression or aneurysm
History of central venous catheter use
Thrombosis localized to catheter insertion site

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe arm swelling and cyanosis
Signs of pulmonary embolism (dyspnea, chest pain)
Progressive limb ischemia or neurological deficits
references: Illig KA, Doyle AJ. A comprehensive review of thoracic outlet syndrome. J Vasc Surg. 2010;51(3):1538-1547.
Peek J, Vos CG, van de Pavoordt HDWM, et al. Venous thoracic outlet syndrome: diagnosis and treatment. J Thorac Dis. 2018;10(Suppl 22):S2639-S2647.
